title: Penang Bridge International Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2025 Edition Was Like
meta_description: Penang Bridge International Marathon review: 23,000+ runners from 64 countries on 14 December 2025, a night race over the Second Bridge from Batu Kawan.
dek: Penang's bridge marathon ran from Batu Kawan across the Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah Bridge on 14 December 2025, with more than 23,000 runners. Here is what that edition was like.
verdict: The Penang Bridge International Marathon is Penang's flagship race and a genuinely hard one. The 2025 edition, on 14 December, drew more than 23,000 participants from 64 countries [1]. Since 2024 it has started and finished at Aspen Vision City in Batu Kawan, crossing the Second Bridge, the Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah Bridge, and back [2]. The state's tourism chairman, himself a runner, described it as one of the toughest races in the region: open stretches, strong crosswinds, elevation changes and a night start [2]. If you want a big, distinctive marathon over a sea bridge, this is the one. Train for wind and climbing.

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition
paragraphs: More than 23,000 participants from 64 countries took part in the Aspen-Klippa Penang Bridge International Marathon on 14 December 2025 [1]. Runners arrived in Batu Kawan from about half past midnight, according to one participant [1].

It was the second year at Aspen Vision City in Batu Kawan, after the state moved the race there in 2024, when it drew about 23,000 runners [2]. There were full marathon, half marathon and 10 km categories, and a special category for visually impaired runners [2].

sections.heading: A Hard Course Over the Second Bridge
paragraphs: The route runs from Aspen Vision City over the Second Bridge and back [2]. Wong Hon Wai, the state tourism chairman and an avid runner, called it the longest bridge marathon in Southeast Asia and one of the toughest races in the region, with open stretches, strong crosswinds, elevation changes and the mental test of running through the night [2].
For 2025 the organisers introduced start pens based on estimated finishing time and an expanded resting area [2].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a big international marathon in Malaysia that is not a city-street race. Crossing a sea bridge at night is the reason to do this one.
Respect the course. Train on hills, expect wind on the bridge, and plan your night: the race starts in the small hours.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2025 edition and the organisers' own description of the course. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: How many people ran the Penang Bridge International Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: More than 23,000 participants from 64 countries took part on 14 December 2025, at Aspen Vision City in Batu Kawan. That was similar to the 23,000 in 2024, the first year at the Batu Kawan venue.

faqs.question: Is the Penang Bridge Marathon course hard?
faqs.answer: Yes. The state tourism chairman described it as one of the toughest races in the region: the Second Bridge has open stretches, strong crosswinds and elevation changes, and the race is run through the night.

faqs.question: Where does the Penang Bridge International Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Since 2024, at Aspen Vision City in Batu Kawan on the mainland. The route crosses the Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah Bridge, Penang's Second Bridge, and returns to Batu Kawan.
